title: Ramayana: Part One opens to an estimated Rs 64.85 crore net in India, trackers say
dek: One tracker's day-one estimate puts the Hindi version at Rs 47.5 crore, with southern-language shows filling more seats. The producers have not released official figures, and trackers disagree.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Ramayana: Part One took an estimated Rs 64.85 crore net at the Indian box office on its opening day, Thursday, according to one tracking site, a strong start for director Nitesh Tiwari's two-part retelling of the epic, though below some of the trade's more bullish forecasts. The producers, Prime Focus Studios and Monster Mind Creations, had not released official figures by early Friday, and other trackers gave lower numbers.

The site's day-end estimate, last updated at 10:06 pm on Thursday, puts the film's India gross at Rs 77.50 crore from about 25,200 shows, with average occupancy of 36%. It estimates that about 25.3 lakh tickets were sold. The figures include 3D surcharges.

## How the languages did

Most of the money came from the Hindi version, according to the same tracker:

- Hindi: Rs 47.50 crore net, 20,678 shows, 31.6% occupancy
- Kannada: Rs 7.25 crore, 60.5% occupancy
- Telugu: Rs 6.00 crore, 58.5% occupancy
- Tamil: Rs 2.60 crore, 44.8% occupancy
- Malayalam: Rs 1.50 crore, 58.2% occupancy

The southern-language versions, with far fewer shows, filled a much larger share of their seats than the Hindi version. Yash, who plays Ravana, is from the Kannada film industry, where the dubbed version had its highest occupancy.

## Why the numbers differ

Box office figures in India are estimates compiled by trackers and trade analysts until a producer publishes its own, and they often disagree on day one. One entertainment site listed the opening at Rs 62.50 crore net. Another outlet estimated about Rs 65 crore net in India and Rs 130-140 crore gross worldwide, and described the start as below the trade's expectations. One earlier report had said that early trade predictions put the worldwide opening at around Rs 160 crore. No tracker had published a verified overseas total by Friday morning. Trackers also differ in method: some count only tickets sold through online platforms and extrapolate the rest, and some report net collections after tax while others report gross, so the figures are not directly comparable.

The film went into release with strong advance sales. Before opening, the same tracking site counted Rs 104.58 crore in advance bookings across its first five days, including blocked seats, of which Rs 41.21 crore was for opening day.

## The film

Ramayana: Part One stars Ranbir Kapoor as Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana, with music by A R Rahman and Hans Zimmer. It runs 195 minutes and was certified "U" for all audiences. It is the first of two parts, and a court filing earlier this week put Part One's budget at Rs 2,000 crore, which would make it one of the most expensive Indian films ever made. The Bombay High Court has granted the producers a dynamic injunction against websites pirating the film.

## What to watch

The first weekend will show whether the film can hold its audience after the opening day. Friday is a working day, so trade analysts will watch Saturday and Sunday collections, and whether the producers publish an official worldwide figure.
